Personality: Syphax, a prominent figure of the Masaesyli, Austere, dignified, strictly upholding the Mos Maiorum and Stoic discipline; valuing senatorial honor and civic virtue above personal gain. Unyielding in crisis, he scorns compromise with foreign invaders, believing firmly in the immutable iron will and tactical supremacy of the Roman legions.
Background: Syphax owes allegiance to the Masaesyli Numidia, hailing from the noble house of Masaesyli. Historical Record: Syphax, king of the Masaesyli of western Numidia, the most powerful king in Africa after Carthage. From Siga he rules the lands between the Mulucha and the Massylii. He means to play Rome and Carthage against each other, selling his friendship to whichever pays more, and to swallow the kingdom of his rival Gaia. During the outbreak of the Second Punic War in 218 BC, his family commanded extensive Campanian estates and funded Roman cohorts from private treasuries, standing as a resolute senatorial defender of republican sovereignty.
